mathematics.independent_solution: Before reading the repaired intent/key/author solution, the retained neutral-wire result gave the complete true set {c}. At any finite exterior radius the ion-rest frame has E=0 and B_phi=mu0*I/(2*pi*r)!=0. The invariant B^2-E^2/c^2 is positive, whereas any B'=0 would make it nonpositive. Thus no subluminal inertial frame removes B even at such an event, and none removes it throughout the exterior. An axial electron-rest boost has B'=gamma*B and moving ions; an axial boost can produce E'=gamma*(v cross B), so E may change. After the independent judgment, the author comparison B'_parallel=B_parallel and B'_perpendicular=gamma*B_perpendicular was found equivalent and correct. All four rationales and their misconception derivations agree.

option_checks.evidence: For the electron-rest axial boost, initial E=0 and B perpendicular to the boost give B'=gamma*B!=0. Positive ions move in that frame and cannot be discarded. Setting only electron current to zero while ignoring ionic current produces the stated false B-removal claim; the second electric-field clause does not rescue the false conjunction.

The ion-rest frame is the stipulated initial frame: electrons still drift, total current is nonzero and B_phi=mu0*I/(2*pi*r)!=0 at finite exterior radii. Equating stationary ions/wire with all charges at rest omits that electronic current. The B-removal assertion is false regardless of the electric-field qualification.

Positive B^2-E^2/c^2 excludes B'=0 in every inertial frame at each finite exterior event. Equivalently, with initial E=0 a boost retains B_parallel and multiplies B_perpendicular by positive gamma, so a nonzero B cannot vanish. For a nonzero axial boost E'=gamma*(v cross B) is nonzero; electric-field components need not be frame independent.

Simultaneous E'=B'=0 would force the nonzero initial field tensor to zero and contradict the positive invariant; it also includes the already impossible B'=0. Macroscopic neutrality cancels rest-frame charge density, not steady current or all electromagnetic sources, so the recorded neutrality-to-no-fields mistake yields a genuinely false alternative.
